chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni narrated from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from al-Qasim ibn Isma'il, from Yahya ibn al-Muthanna, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:
For the Qa'im (peace be upon him) are two occultations; during one of them, he attends the seasons (of pilgrimage), he sees the people but they do not see him.

key_terms.الْمَوَاسِمَ: The seasons (specifically referring to Hajj gatherings)
key_terms.لِلْقَائِمِ: The Awaited Imam (specifically Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Mahdi)
key_terms.وَلَا يَرَوْنَهُ: They do not see him (their perception is limited)
key_terms.يَرَى النَّاسَ: He sees the people (his visibility is latent)

ai.seo_question: What are the two occultations of the Imam al-Qa'im and how did he appear during the first one?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* delineates the two phases of the Twelfth Imam’s occultation, specifically highlighting the 'Minor Occultation' (al-Ghaybah al-Sughra) where he attended Hajj seasons, visible yet unrecognized by the masses. This concept of 'seeing but not seeing' (yura wa la yur) underscores the theological principle of divine concealment (istirar) while maintaining active spiritual guidance, a key tenet in Shia eschatology distinguishing the minor from the major occultation.
